newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares ease 0.1 percent in thin volume.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares ease 0.1 percent in thin volume.

text.p: Istanbul shares eased slightly in quiet trade on Tuesday when the index fluctuated in a tight range of 32 points.
The IMKB National-100 ended down 2 points, or 0.1 percent at 1,953 after running between 1,934 and 1,966.
Daily volume fell to 19.86 trillion lira ($127 million), compared to Monday's 20.57 trillion lira ($ 132.6 million).
"The index moved sideways in a narrow band while investors continued to search for fresh leads," a broker said.
"The market had reacted to Monday's 2.74 percent fall today," said Aykut Ak from Ata Securities.
Ak said investors tended to buy relatively cheaper shares.
"The index remained almost unchanged because state shares were so quiet. Investors are waiting for the new government's moves on economic issues," he said.
Aydin Eroglu from Tat Securities said Tuesday's selective trade, mainly in private sector shares, might be followed by demand for state sector shares.
"Otherwise the index will probably turn down again and test its support at 1,900," Eroglu said.

Of the 247 shares traded, gainers outdid losers by 95 to 91, and 61 remained unchanged. The IMKB Industrial eased 0.16 percent to 1,916, the IMKB Services gained 1.89 percent to 1,888 and the IMKB Financial slightly dropped by 0.48 percent to 2,086.
The index representing the trade sector was the leading gainer with 3.92 percent in a reaction to Monday's 5.95 percent loss.

Actives were led by largely state-owned Turkish Airlines, unchanged at 41,000, media distributor Intermedya Yayincilik, down 450 lira to 4,050 and Investment Company Alarko Gayrimenkul Y.O. up 200 lira to end the day from 6,700.
They made up 17 percent of the total volume.
